items.stem: 'Mix the flour and sugar. Then add two eggs and stir well.' Which type of text is this from?
options: a news report
a diary entry
a poem
a recipe

explain.why: a news report tells what happened, but these lines tell the reader what to do
a diary tells the writer's own day, but these lines give steps
a poem uses rhythm and images, but these lines give steps

solution: The lines are commands in the order they must be done, which is typical of a recipe.

items.stem: 'Dear Grandma, Thank you for the lovely birthday present. I miss you very much.' Which type of text is this from?
options: a recipe
a weather report
a notice
a letter

explain.why: a recipe lists ingredients and steps, which are not here
a weather report describes the weather, which is not here
a notice gives short public information and is not addressed to one person

solution: It begins with 'Dear' and speaks to one person, as a letter does.

items.stem: 'The school library will be closed on Friday for cleaning.' Which type of text is this from?
options: a story
a poem
a diary entry
a notice

explain.why: a story tells about characters and events, but this gives plain information
a poem uses rhythm and images, but this gives plain information
a diary tells the writer's own feelings, but this does not

solution: It gives short, clear information to many readers, as a notice does.

items.stem: 'Once upon a time, a poor fisherman found a golden fish.' Which type of text is this from?
options: a story
a news report
a recipe
an instruction manual

explain.why: a news report tells real events with times and places, but this begins like a tale
a recipe gives steps for cooking, which are not here
an instruction manual tells the reader what to do, which this does not

solution: 'Once upon a time' and a character make this the start of a story.

items.stem: 'Dear Diary, Today was the best day of my life because we won the football match.' Which type of text is this from?
options: a diary entry
a news report
a notice
a recipe

explain.why: a news report is written in the third person, but this is about 'my life'
a notice gives information to many readers, but this shares personal feelings
a recipe gives steps, which are not here

solution: 'Dear Diary' and the writer's own feelings show a diary entry.

items.stem: 'Wash the rice. Add water. Cook for twenty minutes.' What kind of sentences does a recipe mostly use?
options: questions
exclamations
commands
long descriptions

explain.why: a recipe tells readers what to do rather than asking them
a recipe is calm and clear, not full of exclamations
a recipe uses short steps, not long descriptions

solution: Each step tells the reader what to do, so recipes use commands.

items.stem: A poster for a school fun fair says 'JOIN US!' in big bold letters. Why?
options: to explain a science fact
to catch readers' attention
to give a recipe
to tell a long story

explain.why: the words are an invitation, not a fact
the words invite readers to a fair, not give steps
a poster is short and does not tell a long story

solution: Big bold words make people notice the poster.

items.stem: 'It will be sunny with a high of 33 degrees.' Which tense is used mostly in a weather forecast?
options: future tense
past tense
past perfect tense
present perfect tense

explain.why: a forecast is about what will happen, not what has happened
a forecast does not look back at earlier events
a forecast is about the days ahead, not what has just finished

solution: A forecast says what the weather will be, so the future tense is used.

items.stem: Which sentence is most likely from a news report?
options: Wow! You simply must try our brand new chilli crab burger today
Preheat the oven to 180 degrees and grease the baking tray well
I felt my heart pounding loudly as I slowly opened the old door
Two people were taken to hospital after a bus hit a van on Tuesday

explain.why: this is a persuasive advertisement, not a report of events
this is an instruction from a recipe
this is a story told by one character

solution: A news report states facts in the past tense: who, what and when.

items.stem: Which sentence is most likely from an advertisement?
options: The shoes were sold at a shop in Orchard Road on Monday.
Hurry! Buy now and enjoy 20 per cent off all shoes.
Place the shoes in the box and then close the lid firmly.
Ravi quickly laced his shoes and ran towards the school gate.

explain.why: this states a past event, as a news report would
this is an instruction, not a sales message
this is a line from a story

solution: Urgent commands and a special offer are typical of an advertisement.

items.stem: Which sentence is most likely from the instructions for a science experiment?
options: The scientist was excited about her discovery
Pour 100 ml of water into the beaker
Try our new water bottle today
Last week, pupils visited the science centre

explain.why: this describes a person, as a story or report would
this is an advertisement
this is a past event, as in a report

solution: A command with a clear amount and equipment is typical of instructions.

items.stem: An advertisement asks, 'Are you tired of carrying a heavy school bag?' Why does it use this question?
options: to make readers think of a problem the bag solves
to get the reader to reply to the advertiser at once
to give a fact about the size of the school bag
to order the reader to go out and buy the bag

explain.why: it is a rhetorical question, and no reply is expected
it asks about the reader's feeling and does not give a fact
it asks a question and does not give an order

solution: A rhetorical question draws readers in by raising a problem the product will solve.

items.stem: Why does a news report give the time, place and names of people?
options: to build suspense for the reader as in a story
to give facts about who, what, where and when
to persuade readers to buy something at a shop
to describe the feelings of the writer in detail

explain.why: a report aims to inform, not to build suspense
a report informs and does not sell
a report keeps to facts, not personal feelings

solution: These details answer who, what, where and when, so readers get the facts.

items.stem: A letter to the editor says, 'I strongly believe that more trees should be planted in our estate.' Which words show the writer's opinion?
options: more trees
in our estate
I strongly believe
be planted

explain.why: these words name the topic but do not show a belief
these words give the place but do not show a belief
these words describe an action but do not show a belief

solution: 'I strongly believe' tells the reader what the writer thinks.

items.stem: Which feature is more likely to appear in a story than in a recipe?
options: a list of the ingredients needed
numbered steps to follow in order
the characters' spoken words
a list of the tools to be used

explain.why: a list of ingredients belongs to a recipe
numbered steps belong to a recipe
a list of tools belongs to a recipe

solution: Characters speak in a story, and their words go in speech marks.

items.stem: Why does a recipe list the ingredients in a bulleted list?
options: to build suspense about how the food will taste
so readers see what to prepare
to persuade readers to cook the dish tonight
to share the feelings of the writer about food

explain.why: a recipe aims to help the cook, not to build suspense
a list helps readers prepare and does not persuade
a list holds facts and not feelings

solution: A list is easy to scan, so the cook knows what is needed.

items.stem: Which sentence uses a feature typical of a persuasive speech?
options: The bus arrived at 7.45 a.m
Mix the batter until it is smooth
Yesterday, the minister visited a primary school
Surely we all want a greener Singapore

explain.why: this is a plain statement of a fact, not a persuasive feature
this is an instruction, as in a recipe
this reports a past event, as in news

solution: A rhetorical question that makes the audience agree is a persuasive feature.

items.stem: An advertisement says, 'Only three days left! Don't miss out!' What effect do these words create?
options: a sense of urgency
a sense of calm
a sense of sadness
a sense of humour

explain.why: short urgent commands do not make readers feel calm
the words push readers to act, not feel sad
the words are serious, not funny

solution: The deadline and the command press the reader to act quickly.

items.stem: A school report says, 'The recycling drive collected 450 kg of paper in March.' What makes this sentence sound factual?
options: the exact figure and the month
the use of questions
the words that describe feelings
the use of commands

explain.why: there is no question in the sentence
no feelings are described in the sentence
there is no command in the sentence

solution: Exact numbers and dates make a statement checkable and factual.

items.stem: Which sentence is most suitable as the first sentence of an information report about otters?
options: Otters are mammals that live near water
Otters, oh how I love them so very much
Have you ever wished that you could swim like an otter does
One day, an otter named Ollie went for a swim

explain.why: this shows personal feeling, which does not suit an information report
this question suits a persuasive or chatty text, not a report
this begins a story, not a report

solution: An information report opens with a clear general fact about its topic.

items.stem: Why would a writer of a persuasive letter use the words 'must' and 'urgent'?
options: to make the whole letter sound like a story
to press the reader to act
to list steps in order
to add humour to the letter

explain.why: these words do not make a letter into a story
these words do not order steps
these words are serious, not funny

solution: Strong words show how important the matter is and push the reader to act.

items.stem: Which sentence from a story builds suspense through description?
options: The old building has three floors and a small garden.
The floor of the hall is cleaned every Friday.
Visitors may use the stairs on the left side.
The floorboards creaked and a shadow slid across the wall.

explain.why: this states a plain fact and does not build suspense
this states a routine and does not build suspense
this is a notice, not a description in a story

solution: Sounds and moving shadows make the reader feel something is about to happen.

items.stem: A diary says, 'I was so nervous that my hands were shaking.' What does the writer share with the reader?
options: facts in the third person
the writer's own feelings
commands for the reader
statistics about nerves

explain.why: the writer says 'I', so it is first person, not third
the writer does not tell the reader to do anything
there are no numbers or statistics

solution: 'I was so nervous' shares the writer's own feelings.

items.stem: Why does a pupil's letter to the principal say 'I would like to request' instead of 'Can I get'?
options: to make the letter much shorter
to make the letter funny
to sound polite to a formal reader
to tell a story in the letter

explain.why: 'I would like to request' is longer, not shorter
the phrase is polite, not funny
the phrase makes a request and tells no story

solution: A formal reader such as a principal expects polite wording.

items.stem: 'Last night, thieves broke into a shop in Geylang, said the police.' Which type of text is this from?
options: a recipe
a news report
a diary entry
a poem

explain.why: a recipe tells the reader how to cook something
a diary is written by one person about their own day
a poem uses rhythm and images, but this reports an event

solution: It states what happened, where, and who said so, as a news report does.

items.stem: 'This film was funny and exciting. I give it four stars.' Which type of text is this from?
options: a notice
a recipe
a review
a weather forecast

explain.why: a notice gives plain information and does not rate anything
a recipe tells the reader how to cook something
a forecast tells about the weather, not a film

solution: The writer gives an opinion and a rating, as a review does.

items.stem: 'Hi Sam, are you free on Saturday? Let's go cycling!' Which type of text is this from?
options: a news report
a set of instructions
a message to a friend
a poem

explain.why: a news report is about an event and is not addressed to one reader
instructions tell the reader how to do a task
a poem uses rhythm and images, but this invites a friend

solution: It speaks to one friend in a casual way and makes a plan.

items.stem: 'First, put on your helmet. Next, sit on the seat. Finally, push the pedals.' Which type of text is this from?
options: a story
a set of instructions
a poem
a news report

explain.why: a story tells about characters and what happens to them
a poem uses rhythm and images, but these lines give steps
a news report tells what happened, but these lines tell what to do

solution: The steps are in order and tell the reader what to do.

items.stem: Which word is often used to show the order of steps in instructions?
options: However
Because
Next
Although

explain.why: 'However' shows contrast, not order
'Because' gives a reason, not order
'Although' shows contrast, not order

solution: 'Next' shows what step follows.

items.stem: Which sentence is a typical opening of a story?
options: Add two cups of flour to the bowl.
Buy one pair of shoes and get another free.
One rainy afternoon, Mei found a strange key under her bed.
The Prime Minister spoke at the rally on Sunday.

explain.why: this is a step from a recipe
this is a line from an advertisement
this reports an event, as news does

solution: A time, a character and an interesting event start a story.

items.stem: A poster says 'Keep Singapore clean.' What is the purpose of the poster?
options: to remind people to act
to tell a joke
to describe a character
to report the news

explain.why: the words are serious and tell people what to do
there is no character in the words
the words give a request and report nothing

solution: The command reminds readers to do something.

items.stem: Why does a story use words such as 'dark' and 'creepy'?
options: to help the reader picture the scene
to give the reader steps to follow in order
to list facts and figures about the place
to ask the reader a string of questions

explain.why: a story does not give steps
these words describe, they do not give facts
these words are not questions

solution: Describing words help readers see the setting in their mind.

items.stem: A news report has the short headline 'Fire at Toa Payoh flat'. Why is it short?
options: to tell the whole story of the fire in detail
to describe how the writer feels about fires
to give readers a recipe for a good dinner
to tell readers the main news quickly

explain.why: a short line cannot hold the whole story
a headline states the news, not feelings
a headline has nothing to do with a recipe

solution: A short headline gives the main news at a glance.

items.stem: Why does a notice use short, clear sentences?
options: so readers understand it quickly
so readers can enjoy a long story
so readers can guess the ending
so readers can laugh

explain.why: a notice is not a story
a notice has no ending to guess
a notice gives information, not jokes

solution: Short sentences are easy to read at a glance.

items.stem: Which text is mostly written in the past tense?
options: a recipe for fried rice
a forecast for tomorrow
a list of classroom rules
a diary entry about yesterday

explain.why: a recipe uses commands in the present
a forecast uses the future tense
rules use commands and the present tense

solution: A diary about yesterday tells what already happened.

items.stem: Which text would you read to find out how to make a paper aeroplane?
options: a diary entry
a poem
a news report
a set of instructions

explain.why: a diary tells about someone's day
a poem uses rhythm and images
a news report tells what happened

solution: Instructions tell the reader how to make or do something.

items.stem: 'Dear Principal, I am writing to ask if we can have a longer recess.' Which type of letter does this begin?
options: a story
a recipe
a formal letter
a poem

explain.why: a story does not begin with 'Dear Principal'
a recipe does not begin like a letter
a poem is not written like a request to a principal

solution: It addresses a person in authority politely to make a request.

items.stem: Which sign-off is suitable at the end of a letter to a close friend?
options: Your friend, Mei
Yours faithfully
The End
Thank you for reading

explain.why: 'Yours faithfully' is used in formal letters
'The End' closes a story, not a letter
this ends an article or story, not a friendly letter

solution: A friendly sign-off suits a letter to a close friend.

items.stem: Which sentence states a fact?
options: Singapore has the tastiest food.
Singapore became independent in 1965.
Everyone loves living in Singapore.
Singapore is too hot for anyone.

explain.why: 'tastiest' is a personal opinion
'everyone loves' is an opinion that cannot be proved
'too hot' is an opinion that differs from person to person

solution: The year can be checked, so it is a fact.

items.stem: Which sentence states an opinion?
options: Durians are the most delicious fruit.
Durians have a thick, spiky husk.
Durians are sold at many stalls in Geylang.
Durians grow on very tall trees in Johor.

explain.why: this can be checked by looking
this can be checked by visiting stalls
this can be checked by looking at the trees

solution: 'most delicious' depends on taste, so it is an opinion.

items.stem: 'The wind howled angrily.' What does the word 'howled' do?
options: shows how to start a story
gives the exact speed of the wind
tells the reader to run away
makes the wind sound loud and wild

explain.why: a single word does not start a story
'howled' gives a sound, not a number
'howled' is not a command

solution: 'howled' gives the wind a loud, wild sound.

items.stem: In 'Mum said, "It is time for dinner!"', how does the writer show Mum's exact words?
options: with brackets
with bullet points
with speech marks
with a heading

explain.why: brackets add extra information, not speech
bullet points make lists
a heading is a title

solution: Speech marks go around the words a person says.

items.stem: Which text usually has a title, a list of materials and numbered steps?
options: a letter to a friend
a diary entry
instructions for a craft
a poem

explain.why: a letter has a greeting and paragraphs, not numbered steps
a diary has a date and a personal account
a poem has lines and verses, not steps

solution: Craft instructions list what is needed and then give steps.

items.stem: Which feature helps readers find information quickly in a school brochure?
options: long paragraphs
speech marks
rhyming lines
headings and bullet points

explain.why: long paragraphs are slower to scan
speech marks show spoken words
rhyme does not help find facts

solution: Headings and bullet points let readers scan at a glance.

items.stem: Why do news reports use reported speech such as 'The minister said that the park would open next year'?
options: to build suspense for the reader until the end
to give steps for the reader to follow
to tell what someone said without quoting every word
to make the whole report rhyme and sound nice

explain.why: a news report informs, not builds suspense
reported speech does not give steps
reported speech has nothing to do with rhyme

solution: Reported speech passes on what was said in the reporter's own words.

items.stem: Which sentence from a review shows the writer's opinion?
options: The film lasts about two hours in total.
The film was released in cinemas in March.
The cast includes three well-known actors.
I found the plot slow and predictable.

explain.why: the length is a fact
the date is a fact
the number is a fact

solution: 'slow and predictable' is the writer's own judgement.

items.stem: Which text is most likely to have headings such as 'Habitat' and 'Diet'?
options: a story about a puppy that got lost
an information report about an animal
a diary entry about a family trip
an advertisement for pet food

explain.why: a story is told in paragraphs without such headings
a diary has dates, not topic headings
an advertisement is short and persuasive

solution: Headings group facts about a topic in an information report.

items.stem: An advertisement says, 'Imagine waking up to the smell of fresh bread.' What is the advertiser doing?
options: giving steps for baking bread at home
reporting a plain fact about how bread is made
inviting readers to picture a pleasant scene
telling readers a story about a young baker

explain.why: there are no steps in the line
the line is not a statement of fact
there is no character or plot

solution: The word 'Imagine' invites readers to picture something they would enjoy.

items.stem: A speech opens with 'Good morning, principal, teachers and friends.' Why?
options: to give the ending of the speech
to list steps for the audience
to report news about the school
to greet the audience directly

explain.why: this is how a speech starts, not ends
there are no steps here
it greets and does not report anything

solution: A speaker greets the listeners before the speech begins.

items.stem: Why does a story often use the past tense?
options: it gives the reader instructions to follow
it tells events that have already happened
it states facts that are always true everywhere
it makes predictions about what happens tomorrow

explain.why: stories do not instruct
that is the job of the present tense
that would use the future tense

solution: The narrator tells what happened in the story.

items.stem: Why does a writer of instructions use words such as 'carefully' and 'gently'?
options: to build suspense
to tell the reader a secret
to make the text rhyme
to show how to do a step

explain.why: instructions are meant to be clear
these words do not tell a secret
these words are not chosen for rhyme

solution: These adverbs tell the reader the way to do the action.

items.stem: Why do advertisements use words such as 'new', 'free' and 'best'?
options: to make readers want the product
to give the history of the product
to teach readers a skill
to tell a sad story

explain.why: these words say nothing about history
these words do not teach
these words sound happy and sell

solution: These words make the product sound attractive.

items.stem: Which sentence is the topic sentence of a paragraph about recycling?
options: Paper is collected every Tuesday morning.
Blue bins are placed near the lifts.
Many pupils bring bottles from home.
Recycling helps to protect our environment.

explain.why: this is a detail that supports the topic
this is a detail that supports the topic
this is a detail that supports the topic

solution: The topic sentence states the main idea that the details support.

items.stem: Which sentence is the best ending for a letter asking the school to build a bicycle rack?
options: The bicycle has two wheels.
Many pupils like cycling in the park.
I hope you will consider my request.
It rained heavily on Monday.

explain.why: this does not close the letter or the request
this adds a new fact instead of closing
this is not related to the request

solution: A polite closing line repeats the request.

items.stem: Which set of words helps to order events in a recount?
options: however, although, unless
because, since, so
for example, such as, like
first, then, finally

explain.why: these words show contrast or condition
these words show reasons or results
these words give examples

solution: 'first, then, finally' show the order in which things happened.

items.stem: Which tense is mostly used in a recount of a school trip?
options: the future tense
the present continuous tense
the past tense
the present tense for commands

explain.why: the trip has already happened
the trip is not happening now
a recount does not give commands

solution: A recount tells what happened, so it uses the past tense.

items.stem: Why do writers use 'I' in a diary?
options: because they write about their own experience
because they are giving orders to other people
because they are reporting the news to readers
because they are describing a total stranger

explain.why: 'I' is not used to give orders
a news report uses the third person
'I' is the writer, not a stranger

solution: A diary tells the writer's own thoughts and events.

items.stem: Which sentence in a persuasive text gives a reason?
options: Plastic bags are sold at most supermarkets.
I bought a plastic bag at the shop yesterday.
Bags come in many different colours and sizes.
Plastic bags harm sea animals, so we should use them less.

explain.why: this states a fact but gives no reason
this tells what the writer did
this describes bags but gives no reason

solution: 'harm sea animals' is the reason for using fewer bags.

items.stem: A writer says the character 'whispered' instead of 'shouted'. What does 'whispered' show?
options: that the character spoke loudly
that the character was telling a lie
that the character spoke very softly
that the character was far away

explain.why: 'shouted' means loudly, not 'whispered'
'whispered' says nothing about lying
'whispered' says nothing about distance

solution: 'whispered' means to speak in a very quiet voice.

items.stem: 'Her eyes were as bright as stars.' What kind of language is this?
options: a simile
a command
a fact
a question

explain.why: it does not tell anyone to do something
eyes are not really the same as stars
it does not ask anything

solution: A simile compares two things using 'as' or 'like'.

items.stem: 'The classroom was a zoo.' What kind of language is this?
options: a simile
a metaphor
a command
a question

explain.why: a simile uses 'as' or 'like', which are not here
it does not tell anyone to do something
it does not ask anything

solution: A metaphor says one thing is another, without 'as' or 'like'.

items.stem: In 'The balloon burst with a loud bang.', which word imitates a sound?
options: balloon
bang
burst
loud

explain.why: 'balloon' names a thing
'burst' names an action
'loud' describes the sound

solution: 'bang' sounds like the noise it names.

items.stem: Why does the writer use a colon in 'You will need: flour, sugar and eggs'?
options: to show a question
to show spoken words
to introduce a list
to show ownership

explain.why: a question uses a question mark
spoken words use speech marks
ownership uses an apostrophe

solution: A colon introduces a list that follows.

items.stem: A weather report says, 'Showers are expected in the afternoon.' Why does it use 'expected'?
options: because the showers have already stopped
because a forecast cannot be certain
because the writer is telling a story
because the reader must obey

explain.why: 'expected' looks ahead, not back
a forecast is not a story
'expected' is not a command

solution: A forecast says what is likely, not what is sure.

items.stem: Which sentence is written in a formal tone?
options: I would be grateful if you could reply by Friday
Reply fast, okay
Tell me whenever you feel like it
Get back to me soon, please

explain.why: this is casual and blunt
this is casual and vague
this is friendlier but less formal

solution: Polite, full wording is formal.

items.stem: Which sentence is written in an informal tone?
options: I am writing to inform you of a change
Hey, guess what happened today
We regret to announce the closure
Kindly note the new timetable

explain.why: this is formal
this is formal
this is formal

solution: Casual greetings and questions are informal.

items.stem: Why does a persuasive writer say 'We must protect our reefs'?
options: to give the exact number of reefs in the sea
to tell the story of one special reef
to include readers and make them feel part of the cause
to ask readers a question about reefs

explain.why: there is no number in the sentence
the sentence tells no story
the sentence is not a question

solution: 'We' and 'our' bring the reader in as a team member.

items.stem: An essay writer says, 'Many experts agree that exercise is important.' What is the purpose of these words?
options: to make the argument stronger by showing support
to tell a story about a group of experts
to ask the reader a difficult question
to describe what the experts look like

explain.why: the sentence tells no story
the sentence is not a question
no appearance is described

solution: Naming agreement from experts supports the writer's claim.

items.stem: Why does an information report use the present tense, as in 'Otters live near rivers'?
options: because it tells a story from a long time ago
because it gives orders to its readers
because it states general facts that are true now
because it makes plans for the near future

explain.why: a report states facts, not a story
the sentence is not a command
the sentence is not about the future

solution: General facts that stay true are written in the present tense.

items.stem: Why might a writer use short sentences during a chase scene?
options: to slow down the action of the scene
to give a long list of facts
to explain a science idea to readers
to speed up the pace and build tension

explain.why: short sentences make a scene feel faster
a chase scene is not a list
a chase scene tells action

solution: Short sentences feel quick and urgent.

items.stem: A story ends with 'She never saw the old house again.' What does this sentence do?
options: introduces the main character
brings the story to a close
gives a step to follow
asks the reader to reply

explain.why: an introduction comes at the start
a story does not give steps
the sentence is not a question

solution: It tells what happened last, so the story ends.

items.stem: A speaker repeats, 'Never give up! Never give up!' What is the effect?
options: it stresses the message so the audience remembers it
it gives many new facts to the audience
it tells the audience a short story
it makes the speech sound rather uncertain

explain.why: repeating adds no new facts
there is no story in the words
repetition makes it sound firm

solution: Repeating a phrase helps listeners remember it.

items.stem: Which phrase is an exaggeration typical of advertisements?
options: noodles made with wheat flour and water
noodles sold for only two dollars a bowl
the tastiest noodles in the whole universe
noodles served hot with a bowl of soup

explain.why: this is a plain fact
this is a plain fact
this is a plain fact

solution: 'in the whole universe' is too big to be true, so it is an exaggeration.

items.stem: Why do news reports often begin with the most important facts?
options: so the ending is a surprise
so readers do not need the headline
so the report can rhyme
so readers get the main point at once

explain.why: news reports do not aim for a surprise ending
the headline still has a job
rhyme has nothing to do with it

solution: Busy readers see the key facts first.

items.stem: A letter begins 'Dear Sir or Madam'. Which ending is correct?
options: Yours faithfully
Yours sincerely
Love from
See you soon

explain.why: 'Yours sincerely' is for a named person
'Love from' is for family and close friends
'See you soon' is casual

solution: If you do not know the name, close with 'Yours faithfully'.

items.stem: A letter begins 'Dear Mr Tan'. Which ending is correct?
options: Yours faithfully
Love from
See you soon
Yours sincerely

explain.why: 'Yours faithfully' is for an unnamed reader
'Love from' is for family and close friends
'See you soon' is casual

solution: If you know the name, close with 'Yours sincerely'.

items.stem: Which sentence is a recommendation in a book review?
options: The book has about 250 pages in all.
I would recommend this book to anyone who enjoys mysteries.
The author of the book lives in Singapore.
The book was published in Singapore last year.

explain.why: this is a fact about length
this is a fact about the author
this is a fact about its date

solution: The writer advises who should read the book.

items.stem: Why might a writer begin a story with dialogue?
options: to draw the reader straight into the action
to list the main facts of the story first
to explain to readers how to do something
to give readers a short news report

explain.why: dialogue is spoken words, not a list
dialogue does not give steps
dialogue is not news

solution: Spoken words put the reader in the middle of a scene.

items.stem: A diary about a family trip is written mostly in which person?
options: the second person
the third person
all three equally
the first person

explain.why: 'you' is rare in a diary
the writer would say 'he' or 'she' about others only
a diary mainly says 'I' and 'we'

solution: The writer tells 'I' and 'we' experiences.

items.stem: What makes 'Wake up! Step up! Speak up!' memorable?
options: long descriptions of a place
a repeated pattern of short commands
facts and figures about speaking
the past tense of each verb

explain.why: the words are short, not long
there are no facts or figures
the verbs are commands, not past tense

solution: Repeating a pattern makes words easy to remember.

items.stem: Why does a museum brochure include opening hours and ticket prices?
options: to give practical information visitors need
to tell a story about how the museum began
to describe how the objects look inside
to make the whole brochure rhyme nicely

explain.why: these details are not a story
these details are not about objects
these details are not for rhyme

solution: Visitors need these facts to plan a visit.

items.stem: Which sentence shows the writer's stance clearly in a persuasive essay on homework?
options: Yesterday I finished my homework at nine o'clock.
Homework is work that teachers give to pupils.
Homework takes up too much of our time, and it is time for a change.
Once upon a time, a boy hated his homework.

explain.why: this recounts what the writer did
this defines the word and takes no stance
this starts a story

solution: It says clearly what the writer wants.

items.stem: Which sentence uses a statistic to support an argument?
options: Many of the pupils feel tired after school.
Nine out of ten pupils in our school said they felt tired after a long day.
Pupils sometimes feel tired in the afternoon.
Some of our pupils feel very tired.

explain.why: 'many' gives no number
'sometimes' gives no number
'some' gives no number

solution: 'Nine out of ten' is a number that backs up the claim.

items.stem: Why does a news report put a quotation in speech marks?
options: to show that the words are meant as a joke
to show these are the speaker's exact words
to show a list of items in the report
to show the title of the whole report

explain.why: speech marks do not mean a joke
a list is not shown with speech marks
a title does not need speech marks

solution: Speech marks show the exact words someone said.
